problem: Venezuelans face fragmented payments, dollar and remittance access, and unreliable delivery; merchants lack online presence and logistics.
business_model: Marketplace and delivery fees, payments, and SaaS for merchants (QUIK Pro)
product_category: Super app: payments wallet, delivery marketplace, merchant software

founders.name: Alejandro Flores-Hernandez
founders.background_notes: YC page: over 10 years as field service engineer installing gas turbines. Bloomberg Linea describes him as a 35-year-old engineer from Maracaibo.

founders.name: Mauricio Martínez
founders.background_notes: YC page: graphic designer, art director, marketer, project manager with 10 years experience.

competitors.name: Yummy
competitors.what: Venezuelan delivery and payments super app

technical_complexity.rationale: Multi-sided app with wallet, multi-currency payments and logistics operations in a country with payment and infrastructure limits.

defensibility.rationale: Local merchant and courier network helps but a funded rival (Yummy) already pursued the same super app idea.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: An aggregator claims an unnamed M&A offer in April 2025; unverified. Company remained active.

market_need_then: Bloomberg Linea (March 2022) reported about 40,000 users in Maracaibo and demand for QR payments, a dollar-friendly wallet and delivery.

branding.domain_note: Company site is quikpago.com (suffix), not quik.com.
branding.community_and_virality: Bloomberg Linea ran a story on being the first Maracaibo startup in YC.

brand_strength.rationale: Local press interest but name collides with Qik (Dominican bank) and other Quik brands; no brand-specific evidence.

outcome_analysis: QUIK built a Maracaibo-based payments and delivery app that reached about 40,000 users by March 2022, expanded to Caracas, and is listed active with a 20-person team. Founders are local, which helps with merchant and courier access. No funding round could be verified from a primary source, so the funding story is incomplete. No shutdown or confirmed sale was found.
notes: Unverified: CB Insights lists $500K convertible note on 2022-03-29; Bloomberg Linea says founders were raising about $3M. An aggregator mentions an April 2025 M&A offer, unsourced. quikpago.com fetch was rate-limited by the safety check. Name origin not found. Revenue and headcount claims from secondary sources not recorded. Completeness pass: the $500K convertible note dated 2022-03-29 rests on a single database (CB Insights); Bloomberg Linea says the founders were raising about $3M, and GetLatka claims the company is bootstrapped, so the full history is unknown.
